newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside says plans to shut Cossack.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside says plans to shut Cossack.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Monday it plans to halt production of crude oil at the Cossack Pioneer oil rig at around 1000 GMT (six p.m. local time) on Monday because of an approaching cyclone.
A Woodside spokesman said it plans to disconnect the rig from its mooring in the Indian ocean offshore of Western Australia before leaving the vicintity to avoid the path of cyclone Rachel.

The rig, which only resumed production at a rate of around 90,000 barrels a day last weekend after being shut since December 31 becuase of cyclone Phil will remain detached from its mooring until the cyclone passes, the spokesman said.

At 0400 GMT (midday local), cyclone Rachel was estimated to be 200 km west of the coastal town of Broome and 300 km northeast of Port Hedland, traveling west-southwest at 15 km an hour, the Bureau of Meteorology said.
"We're still keeping an eye on it, but the plan is to shut production at about six tonight," the spokesman told Reuters.
The bureau earlier on Monday issued a warning for a category two-sized cyclone but now says it expects to upgrade Rachel to category three on Monday evening.
A category three cyclone carries winds between 170 and 224 kms an hour.
The Cossack Pioneer pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields on the North West Shelf of the Indian Ocean.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf project are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron Corp, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
